## AIActivationManager

`res://assets/scripts/game_mode/AIActivationManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Switches AI pawns off when the ground around them isn't loaded, back on when it is, and sets how often the rest run.

A module of GameMode (GameMode.ai_activation_manager), server or offline only. An AI pawn runs only while every chunk within `edge_margin` of it is built; a pawn that keeps the world loaded (`Pawn.is_keeping_world_loaded()`) is always left on, and a possession is checked at once. A pawn that's off stops its NetworkEntity and TickState and is left out of snapshots. Pawns register with `add_pawn()` and `remove_pawn()` (Pawn does both) and need a `set_frozen(frozen)`.

It also sets `Pawn.tick_step` for each running AI pawn: every tick within `full_rate_within_chunks` chunks of the nearest viewer (pawns a player has, and this machine's player's camera), every 2nd up to `every_4th_tick_beyond_chunks`, every 4th beyond, and never less often than TickDriver.load_step. Distance is in whole chunk rings, not metres, so pawns in one chunk share a rate. A pawn a player has always runs every tick. A game can listen to `ai_deactivated` and `ai_activated` to simulate switched-off pawns more cheaply. Design: pawn spec 8.21, scaling spec 7.1.

### Settings and properties

- `edge_margin: float` = `2.0`: How close a pawn may get to unbuilt ground, in metres. It has to be further than the pawn moves between its checks, about 0.5 m for a walking pawn at the default of 6 ticks.
- `spread_over_ticks: int` = `6`: Each pawn is checked once in this many ticks (physics frames without the tick driver), so a big horde isn't all checked at once.
- `max_checks_per_tick: int` = `500`: The most pawns checked in one tick, however many there are. A very large horde takes longer to get through, so with a lot of fast pawns, raise edge_margin too. A removed chunk is always handled at once, so this only delays walking to an edge.
- `steps_by_distance: bool` = `true`: On, AI pawns far from every viewer run every 2nd or 4th tick (pawn spec 8.21). Off, distance changes nothing (the load ladder still applies).
- `full_rate_within_chunks: float` = `2.0`: Within this many chunks of the nearest viewer, an AI pawn runs every tick. Counted in whole rings of chunks.
- `every_4th_tick_beyond_chunks: float` = `4.0`: Beyond this many chunks of the nearest viewer, every 4th tick; between the two, every 2nd.

### Signals

- `ai_deactivated(pawn: Node3D)`: Sent when a pawn is switched off, because the ground around it isn't loaded.
- `ai_activated(pawn: Node3D)`: Sent when a pawn is switched back on.

### Functions

- `get_match_options() -> PackedStringArray`: The settings a start menu may offer (GameModeModule.get_match_options).
- `add_pawn(pawn: Node3D) -> void`: Starts watching a pawn. Adding the same one twice does nothing.
- `remove_pawn(pawn: Node3D) -> void`: Stops watching a pawn, such as one leaving the tree. If it was off, it goes back on.
- `is_active(pawn: Node3D) -> bool`: False while this pawn is switched off.
- `get_step_counts() -> Dictionary`: How many watched pawns run at each step now, for diagnostics: {1: n, 2: n, 4: n}. Frozen pawns aren't counted.
- `get_inactive_count() -> int`: How many pawns are off right now.
- `get_watched_count() -> int`: How many pawns are watched, on or off.
- `step_for(pawn: Node3D) -> int`: How often this pawn should run now: 1 (every tick), 2 or 4. See the class description.
- `_has_ground_around(at: Vector3) -> bool`: True if some terrain has all the chunks around this position, or if there are no terrains to ask.
- `_refresh_terrains() -> void`: Finds the terrains again, and listens for chunks going away on any new ones.
- `_on_chunk_removed(_key: Vector2i) -> void`: A pawn could be standing on it, and can't wait for its turn in the staggered checks. During a tick (chunks unload in before_tick, at most one a tick) everyone is checked at once, before the tick runs; without the tick driver, at the next check.

## GameModeModule

`res://assets/scripts/game_mode/GameModeModule.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

The base for one optional piece of a game's rules, added to GameMode.

Extend it, and override what's useful. A module with no per-frame work should switch off its own _process, because Godot runs it for any script that defines it.

### Functions

- `_on_module_added(_game_mode: GameModeSingleton) -> void`: Just added. Fill in your line on GameMode here, if you have one, such as game_mode.ai_activation_manager = self.
- `_on_module_removed(_game_mode: GameModeSingleton) -> void`: About to be removed. Clear your line on GameMode here, and undo anything you've changed in the world.
- `get_match_options() -> PackedStringArray`: The names of this module's settings (its @exports) a start menu may offer before a match; MatchOptionsPanel lists them. Empty: none.

## PawnInitializer

`res://assets/scripts/game_mode/PawnInitializer.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Gives every pawn the parts it needs to work, from one list per game.

A module of GameMode (GameMode.pawn_initializer). A Pawn calls `initialize()` from its _enter_tree; for each part in the
defaults file, in order, it adds the part unless the pawn already has a child of that name. So a designer overrides a default by
putting their own part with that name in the scene, and every machine gets the same names in the same order. The defaults are
resources/pawn_defaults.tres (a [`PawnDefaultsRes`](../resources/REFERENCE.md#pawndefaultsres)) or the file named by the project setting
`project_base/game_mode/pawn_defaults`. It never adds TickStateComponent or NetworkEntity: NetworkSession reads them
before the pawn joins the tree, so they stay in the scene.

To opt out: Pawn.fill_in_default_parts off (one pawn, every default), Pawn.skip_default_parts (some), or leave this module out of
GameMode (the whole game). Design: pawn spec 11.

### Settings and properties

- `defaults: PawnDefaultsRes` = `null`: The defaults in use. Read from the file when the module starts. A test or a game can set its own.

### Constants

- `DEFAULTS_SETTING = "project_base/game_mode/pawn_defaults"`: The project setting naming the defaults file, if a game uses another.
- `DEFAULT_DEFAULTS_PATH = "res://assets/scripts/resources/pawn_defaults.tres"`: The defaults file used without that setting.

### Functions

- `initialize(pawn: Pawn) -> void`: Adds each default part this pawn doesn't have yet. The pawn calls this from its _enter_tree.
- `part_name_of(scene: PackedScene) -> StringName` *(static)*: The name a part gets on the pawn: its scene's root node name. Read without making the scene.

## PossessionCoordinator

`res://assets/scripts/game_mode/PossessionCoordinator.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Who controls which pawn: players possess and let go of pawns through here.

A module of GameMode (GameMode.possession_coordinator). It creates this machine's PlayerController at the start, which lasts the whole game with or without a pawn. The possessable flag on the pawn's ControllerManager is the check. In multiplayer the server decides and a client's call is only a request; a possessed pawn's owner_peer is its player (0 on letting go, so the server runs it). The pawn's ControllerManager hears of it through possession_changed and its AIController takes over. Respawning or removing a pawn belongs to the game, which can listen to `released`.

```gdscript
GameMode.possession_coordinator.possess(pawn)            # offline, or a client asking the server
GameMode.possession_coordinator.possess_for(peer, pawn)  # server: gives this player this pawn
GameMode.possession_coordinator.spectate()               # lets go and flies a FreeFlyCamera; possessing stops it
```

Spectating is local: only this machine knows its player is spectating, and the spectator is a FreeFlyCamera, not a Pawn. Design: pawn spec 6.2.

### Settings and properties

- `controller: PlayerController` = `null`: This machine's controller. A dedicated server build has none.

### Signals

- `possessed(peer: int, pawn: Pawn)`: A player has a pawn now. On a client, this fires for every player, not only this one.
- `released(peer: int, pawn: Pawn)`: A player has let go of a pawn, or lost it.
- `refused(peer: int, pawn: Pawn, reason: String)`: A request was turned down, on the machine that decided.
- `spectating_changed(spectating: bool)`: This machine's player started or stopped spectating.

### Constants

- `CONTROLLER_SCENE_SETTING = "project_base/game_mode/player_controller_scene"`: A project setting: a scene to use as the PlayerController, so a game can have its own.
- `OFFLINE_PEER = -1`: How offline play refers to its one player, since it has no network peer number.
- `CHANNEL = "possession"`: The world channel the server tells clients who has which pawn on.
- `REQUEST_CHANNEL = "possession_request"`: The client channel a client asks the server for a pawn on.
- `MESSAGE_ONE = 1`
- `MESSAGE_ALL = 2`

### Functions

- `possess(pawn: Pawn) -> bool`: Takes a pawn for this machine's player. Offline it happens now. On a client it's a request, so it may be turned down. On a server with a local player, that player is peer 1. Returns false if it's refused straight away.
- `release() -> void`: Lets go of this machine's pawn. On a client it's a request.
- `spectate() -> bool`: Lets go of this machine's pawn, if it has one (its AI controller takes over), and flies the spectator, starting where the camera is. On a client, letting go is a request, but the flying starts at once. False with no PlayerController (a dedicated server).
- `stop_spectating() -> void`: Stops flying the spectator. The camera holds where it is until this machine's player has a pawn. Possessing one stops spectating by itself, so this is only needed to stop without one.
- `is_spectating() -> bool`: True while this machine's player is flying the spectator.
- `possess_for(peer: int, pawn: Pawn) -> bool`: Server or offline: gives this player this pawn, and takes away the one they had. False means refused.
- `release_for(peer: int) -> void`: Server or offline: this player lets go. The pawn stays, with nobody driving it unless something else takes over.
- `release_pawn(pawn: Pawn) -> void`: Server or offline: whoever has this pawn lets go of it. This is the only way to evict someone. Turning possessable off doesn't: it only stops new possessions.
- `get_pawn_of(peer: int = 0) -> Pawn`: Which pawn a player has. With no peer given, this machine's player.
- `get_peer_of(pawn: Pawn) -> int`: Which player has this pawn, or 0 if none does.
- `_catch_up_message() -> PackedByteArray`: Server: what a late joiner needs to know.
- `_on_network_message(bytes: PackedByteArray) -> void`: Client: the server says who has what.
- `_ask_server(entity_id: int) -> void`: Client: asks the server for a pawn, by id. 0 means let go. The server can say no.
- `_on_request(peer: int, bytes: PackedByteArray) -> void`: Server: a client asks for a pawn. A client can send anything, so the size is checked and the usual checks apply.
- `_on_player_leaving(peer: int) -> void`: Server: a player has gone. Letting go sets the pawn's owner to 0, so NetworkSession doesn't remove it with the rest of what they owned. AIActivationManager switches it off if its ground unloads, like any pawn with no player.

## SpawnManager

`res://assets/scripts/game_mode/SpawnManager.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

Puts pawns into the world at SpawnPoints, and brings players back after they die.

A module of GameMode (GameMode.spawn_manager), like Unreal's GameMode picking a PlayerStart. With no spawn points placed it does nothing. Server or offline only. Type names are NetworkSession's (register_type), so every spawned pawn exists on every machine; a pawn's team comes from its scene. Delays count ticks on TickDriver and run between ticks, so pausing the driver pauses them.

```gdscript
GameMode.spawn_manager.spawn("goblin", &"red_base")     # at a point in that group
GameMode.spawn_manager.spawn_near("goblin", node, 3.0)  # within 3 m of a node (PawnSpawner uses this)
GameMode.spawn_manager.spawn_player(peer)               # possessed for them, and brought back when it dies
```

Points are chosen by team and group, shuffled with the tick's random numbers (repeatable); the first free spot wins (README).

### Settings and properties

- `respawn_players: bool` = `true`: On: players' pawns come back after dying.
- `player_respawn_ticks: int` = `180`: How long a player's pawn stays dead, in ticks at 60 a second (180: 3 s).
- `player_respawn_at_spawn_point: bool` = `true`: On: a player's pawn comes back at a spawn point for its team. Off, or with no point: where it fell.
- `tries_per_point: int` = `4`: How many spots inside a point's scatter_radius it tries before going on to the next point.
- `clearance_radius: float` = `0.6`: How close another pawn's body may be to a new pawn's middle, in metres, for the spot to count as free.
- `ground_lift: float` = `0.3`: How far above the ground a pawn appears on terrain, in metres, so it never starts inside it.
- `pawn_layers: int` = `2`: The physics layers pawns are on, for the free-spot check. Pawns use layer 2.
- `claim_ticks: int` = `2`: For how many ticks a spot it handed out counts as taken, until physics has stepped and sees the pawn there itself. 2 covers a frame that runs two ticks.
- `max_spawns_per_tick: int` = `1`: The most pawns spawners ([`PawnSpawner`](../spawning/REFERENCE.md#pawnspawner)) may spawn in one tick; the rest wait for the next ticks, so a wave or a burst of replacements is spread out instead of landing in one frame (a pawn costs about 10 ms to spawn). 0: no limit. Players' pawns (`spawn_player()`) are never held back, but count towards it.

### Signals

- `pawn_spawned(pawn: Pawn)`: Sent on the server or offline for every pawn this manager spawns.
- `player_respawned(peer: int, pawn: Pawn)`: Sent when a player's pawn comes back after dying.

### Constants

- `RANDOM_SALT = 7151`: Separates these rolls from other users of the same tick's random numbers (DeterministicRandom).

### Functions

- `get_match_options() -> PackedStringArray`: The settings a start menu may offer (GameModeModule.get_match_options).
- `spawn(type_name: String, group: StringName = &"", owner_peer: int = 0) -> Pawn`: Spawns a pawn of this type at a point its team may use, in this group (or any group, with &""). owner_peer is whose input it follows, 0 for the server's own. Returns the pawn, or null if there's no point or this machine can't spawn.
- `spawn_near(type_name: String, around: Node3D, scatter_radius: float, owner_peer: int = 0) -> Pawn`: Spawns a pawn of this type within scatter_radius of a node, facing the node's way, with no spawn point needed. PawnSpawner uses this when it has no group of points.
- `spawn_player(peer: int, type_name: String = "pawn", group: StringName = &"") -> Pawn`: A player's pawn: spawned at a point for its team, possessed for this player, and brought back when it dies (respawn_players). peer is the player's network peer; offline, anything (it's possessed for the one local player).
- `find_place(team: int, group: StringName = &"") -> Dictionary`: Where a pawn of this team would appear, asked for with this group: {"position": Vector3, "yaw": float}, or {} with no point. See "How a spawn point is chosen" in the README.
- `after_ticks(ticks: int, what: Callable) -> void`: Runs what after this many ticks (at 60 a second, converted to the match's rate), booked with the tick scheduler: it runs just before the tick it's due on, between ticks. Pausing the tick driver pauses the count. For delays that are part of the game's rules, such as respawns and body removal.
- `_free_spot(world_node: Node3D, centre: Vector3, yaw: float, radius: float) -> Dictionary`: A free spot near this centre, or {}. The node is only for its physics world.
- `_spot(centre: Vector3, yaw: float, radius: float) -> Dictionary`: A spot inside the circle, on the ground if there's terrain.
- `_ground_height(at: Vector3) -> float`: The height a pawn appears at here: on terrain, just above the ground (building that chunk first if it isn't yet, since the server may have no ground there); without terrain, the height it was given.
- `_is_free(world_node: Node3D, feet: Vector3) -> bool`: True if no pawn body is within clearance_radius of a new pawn's middle here, and no spot handed out lately is within twice clearance_radius (two pawns' worth), since physics doesn't see those pawns yet.
- `_claim(feet: Vector3) -> void`: Remembers a spot a pawn was just put on, for claim_ticks ticks (see the README).
- `_team_of(type_name: String) -> int`: A pawn type's team, read from its scene once: an instance is made, read and freed, without entering the tree.
- `spawns_left_this_tick() -> int`: How many more pawns spawners may spawn this tick (`max_spawns_per_tick`); a large number with no limit.

## TeamRegistry

`res://assets/scripts/game_mode/TeamRegistry.gd`, extends [`Node`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/classes/class_node.html)

How many pawns are on each team, kept current as pawns enter and leave the tree and change team.

A module of GameMode (GameMode.team_registry). AI sensing asks it whether anyone is on another team at all, and skips looking when nobody is (pawn spec 10.4). It counts the pawns in Pawn.GROUP when it starts, then follows the tree's node_added and node_removed and each pawn's team_changed. Without this module nothing breaks: sensing just looks every time.

### Functions

- `count_on_team(team: int) -> int`: How many pawns in the tree are on this team.
- `count_not_on_team(team: int) -> int`: How many pawns in the tree are on any team but this one. AI sensing skips looking when it's 0.
- `get_counts() -> Dictionary`: Every team with pawns on it, and how many: a copy, so changing it changes nothing here.
